answer.rationale: p99 latency on write path is spiking under heavy settlement load at daily peak. The security patch must stay; rollback is ruled out. Routing read traffic to replicas (memory_b5) freed write path capacity in a similar heavy-load scenario and recovered latency same-day. Regional failover is viable backup (memory_b2) but read replica routing is lower-risk, faster, and targets the root contention without moving traffic. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect against cascading failure but don't solve capacity saturation. Capacity provisioning (memory_b3) takes time we don't have. A standard experiment scope on replica routing lets us measure impact in real-time during peak; if it doesn't relieve pressure within 10 minutes, we can escalate to failover while preserving the security patch.
